title: 富兰克林邓普顿Larry：中期选举若变天，AI板块面临回调压力？
speaker: Larry Hathaway

segments.en: as a result of these things. Larry, you mentioned the US midterms. I'm just wondering what your expectations was.
segments.zh: 由于这些因素。拉里，你提到了美国中期选举。我想知道你的预期是什么。

segments.en: What this could mean for markets. If in fact, we do see a sort of democratic sweep, obviously, AI regulation could be that mechanism here
segments.zh: 这对市场可能意味着什么。如果事实上，我们确实看到某种民主党大胜，显然，人工智能监管可能成为这里的机制

segments.en: that could potentially hurt this AI rally we're seeing.
segments.zh: 这可能会损害我们看到的这轮人工智能上涨。

segments.en: What sort of implications do you think that the midterms are going to have on markets?
segments.zh: 你认为中期选举将对市场产生什么样的影响？

segments.en: Right, so I think you're pointing the right direction. In other words, to some extent, at least the Democrats resting back control of the House
segments.zh: 对，所以我认为你指对了方向。换句话说，至少在某种程度上，民主党重新控制众议院

segments.en: is now arguably a known known. That is, it's widely predicted by both the polls and by prediction markets.
segments.zh: 现在可以说是已知的已知。也就是说，民调和预测市场都广泛预测了这一点。

segments.en: The Senate still remains, I suppose, more of a question mark.
segments.zh: 参议院仍然，我想，更像是一个问号。

segments.en: And then there are some questions around some of the state local elections.
segments.zh: 然后还有一些关于州和地方选举的问题。

segments.en: There are a variety of issues that are driving that. One, of course, is the traditional factor that in midterms and the incumbents tend to be challenged and tend to lose seats.
segments.zh: 有多种问题在推动这一点。当然，一个是传统因素，在中期选举中，现任者往往受到挑战，往往失去席位。

segments.en: In that case, that's the Republicans at the moment.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，目前是共和党。

segments.en: But there are, of course, concerns about affordability, which I touched upon a moment ago.
segments.zh: 但当然，人们对负担能力的担忧是存在的，我刚才也提到了这一点。

segments.en: The third factor, though, is that there is somewhat bipartisan.
segments.zh: 不过，第三个因素是，这在一定程度上是两党共同的问题。

segments.en: It shows up by partisan fashion opposition to the rapid build out, the AI centers.
segments.zh: 它表现为两党对人工智能中心快速建设的反对。

segments.en: And in particular, their impacts on, let's say, local economies.
segments.zh: 尤其是它们对当地经济的影响。

segments.en: These are large scale projects in many cases that have been going through accelerated approval processes.
segments.zh: 这些项目在许多情况下规模庞大，一直通过加速审批流程推进。

segments.en: That's created a bit of backlash. And there's a perception, of course, that they're also leading to higher prices for electricity through utility rates.
segments.zh: 这引发了一些反弹。当然，人们还认为，这些项目通过公用事业费率导致电价上涨。

segments.en: And that, of course, is a concern for many voters in different parts of the country.
segments.zh: 当然，这是全国不同地区许多选民关心的问题。

segments.en: It's possible that, if that manifests, not only, again, at the federal level but at the state local level in terms of the election outcome,
segments.zh: 如果这种情况在联邦层面以及州和地方层面的选举结果中体现出来，

segments.en: that could lead to some slowing of the approval processes around that AI build out story.
segments.zh: 那可能会导致人工智能建设相关的审批流程有所放缓。

segments.en: That said, I think there is, obviously, still a lot to be said for the jobs that come with that build out, especially in areas of construction
segments.zh: 话虽如此，我认为显然还是要强调建设带来的就业机会，尤其是在建筑领域。

segments.en: and in other dimensions of the economy.
segments.zh: 以及经济的其他方面。

segments.en: So I think it's finally balanced. I don't think that it's going to lead to a significant sort of backlash nor necessarily significant market set back as a result of the elections.
segments.zh: 所以我认为最终是平衡的。我不认为这会导致严重的反弹，也不一定会因选举而导致显著的市场倒退。
